title: Impact of Peer Ability on Academic Performance

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS).
- Why: Peer (roommate) ability affecting a student’s GPA is endogenous due to sorting, reflection, and correlated unobservables. We use the assigned roommate’s ability (z) as an instrument for peer ability exposure (x), while controlling for demographics and prior performance (controls).
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: Assignment to a higher-ability roommate (z) increases peer ability exposure (strong first stage).
  - Exclusion: z affects the student’s GPA only through peer ability, not via other channels (no direct effect).
  - Independence: Conditional on controls, roommate assignment is as good as random.
  - Monotonicity/SUTVA: No defiers; no spillovers across rooms other than the assigned roommate.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required packages (install if missing)
pkgs <- c("AER","sandwich","lmtest")
for (p in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  }
}
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Read data
dat <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s81_data.csv")

# Quick sanity check
stopifnot(all(c("y","x","z","controls") %in% names(dat)))

# 2) Naive OLS (for comparison)
ols1 <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = dat)
ols1_rob_vcov <- vcovHC(ols1, type = "HC1")
ols1_ct <- coeftest(ols1, vcov = ols1_rob_vcov)

# 3) 2SLS: instrument x with z, include controls as exogenous regressors
iv1 <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | controls + z, data = dat)
iv1_rob_vcov <- vcovHC(iv1, type = "HC1")
iv1_ct <- coeftest(iv1, vcov = iv1_rob_vcov)

# Extract main coefficient and inference (IV with controls)
iv_beta <- coef(iv1)["x"]
iv_se   <- sqrt(diag(iv1_rob_vcov))["x"]
iv_t    <- iv_beta / iv_se
iv_df   <- df.residual(iv1)
iv_p    <- 2 * pt(abs(iv_t), df = iv_df, lower.tail = FALSE)
iv_ci_l <- iv_beta + qt(0.025, df = iv_df) * iv_se
iv_ci_u <- iv_beta + qt(0.975, df = iv_df) * iv_se

# 4) First-stage strength: x on z and controls (robust partial F via t^2 for z)
fs1 <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = dat)
fs1_ct <- coeftest(fs1, vcov = vcovHC(fs1, type = "HC1"))
# Robust t for instrument z (single instrument, so t^2 is robust partial F)
t_z <- as.numeric(fs1_ct["z","t value"])
F_robust <- t_z^2

# 5) Robustness checks
# (a) IV without controls
iv2 <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = dat)
iv2_rob_vcov <- vcovHC(iv2, type = "HC1")
iv2_beta <- coef(iv2)["x"]
iv2_se   <- sqrt(diag(iv2_rob_vcov))["x"]
iv2_t    <- iv2_beta / iv2_se
iv2_df   <- df.residual(iv2)
iv2_p    <- 2 * pt(abs(iv2_t), df = iv2_df, lower.tail = FALSE)

# (b) OLS without controls
ols2 <- lm(y ~ x, data = dat)
ols2_ct <- coeftest(ols2, vcov = vcovHC(ols2, type = "HC1"))
ols2_beta <- coef(ols2)["x"]
ols2_se   <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(ols2, type = "HC1")))["x"]
ols2_p    <- 2 * pt(abs(ols2_beta/ols2_se), df = df.residual(ols2), lower.tail = FALSE)

# 6) Print clear numerical results
cat("=== Main 2SLS (x instrumented by z; controls included) ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Peer ability effect (beta_hat on x): %.4f\n", iv_beta))
cat(sprintf("Robust SE: %.4f | t: %.2f | df: %d | p-value: %.4f\n", iv_se, iv_t, iv_df, iv_p))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n", iv_ci_l, iv_ci_u))

cat("First-stage strength (x ~ z + controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("Robust t-stat for z: %.2f | Robust partial F: %.2f\n\n", t_z, F_robust))

cat("=== Comparison/Robustness ===\n")
cat(sprintf("OLS with controls (coef on x): %.4f | Robust SE: %.4f | p-value: %.4f\n",
            ols1_ct["x","Estimate"], sqrt(diag(ols1_rob_vcov))["x"], ols1_ct["x","Pr(>|t|)"]))
cat(sprintf("2SLS without controls (coef on x): %.4f | Robust SE: %.4f | p-value: %.4f\n",
            iv2_beta, iv2_se, iv2_p))
cat(sprintf("OLS without controls (coef on x): %.4f | Robust SE: %.4f | p-value: %.4f\n",
            ols2_beta, ols2_se, ols2_p))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Being exposed to higher-ability roommates should raise a student’s GPA.
- Magnitude: For standardized measures, a 1 SD increase in peer ability is typically associated with a 0.10–0.30 SD increase in GPA. IV estimates may be larger than OLS if OLS suffers attenuation or negative selection bias. Robust first-stage F-stat should exceed conventional thresholds (e.g., >10).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use assigned roommate ability as an instrument for peer quality.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: A positive causal relationship between peer ability and student GPA is identified.
